title: Subtask block
description: Schema for each entry in the YAML `## Subtasks` block of plan.md. Written by the planner; read by the orchestrator (for scheduling and scope enforcement) and by implementers (as their assignment).

id.description: e.g. st-2-combat-hooks. Stable for the life of the task.

goal.description: One sentence an implementer can act on without reading the rest of the plan.

file_scope.description: Write scope: globs this subtask may modify. Enforced — out-of-scope hunks are flagged at review. Be precise; an over-broad scope defeats parallel safety.

reads.description: Files this subtask depends on but must not modify.

depends_on.description: Subtask ids that must complete first. Empty means it can start immediately.

hotspots.description: Unmergeable or high-coupling files this subtask must touch (engine scenes, project settings, central modules). Taken as exclusive locks.

frozen_interfaces.description: Exact signatures/signals this subtask must expose for others to code against. Changing one later is a major deviation.

estimated_loc.description: Rough changed-line estimate. It is the baseline the implementer measures its own scope_overrun signal against (references/escalation.md), so an honest number matters more than a flattering one. Nothing else is computed from it.

acceptance.description: Acceptance criteria from task.md this subtask satisfies. Every AC in task.md must be claimed by at least one subtask.

test_notes.description: How this should be verified, and whether the checks are fast (engine-free) or slow.

tier.description: Which capability band should run this job. t1 cheap and fast, t2 the workhorse, t3 the strongest enrolled. The registry maps each band to a model and a default provider. Advisory: a band nothing enrolled can serve is logged and demoted rather than parking the run.
